text_blocks.snippet: Squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is a type of cancer that develops from squamous cells, which are flat cells found in the outer layer of the skin. It's the second most common type of skin cancer and can also occur in other parts of the body like the lungs and head and neck region. SCC can appear as a scaly, red patch, a raised bump, or an open sore that doesn't heal.

list.title: Location:
list.snippet: Primarily found on sun-exposed areas of the skin, but can also occur in other locations like the lungs, head and neck, and genitals.

list.title: Appearance:
list.snippet: May manifest as a rough, scaly, red patch, an open sore, a wart-like growth, or a brown spot.
